Figure 2:Overview of GOLD-SLAM. The UAV platform collects LiDAR, IMU measurements and panoramic images.
Inspired by FAST-LIVO2’s error-state filtering framework[32], the frontend integrates panoramic visual updates with IMU propagation and LiDAR scan-to-map constraints.
Inter-frame constraints use features in the LiDAR blind zone, while Patch Brightness Uncertainty (PBU) models shared brightness variations in the LiDAR-supported zone.
To support panoramic reconstruction, we adapt the Gaussian-LIC2 backend[13]to spherical projection and rendering.
Gaussians are initialized using measured LiDAR depth and predicted panoramic depth, and optimized with photometric and LiDAR depth losses.
Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP) combines depth-aware insertion, depth-guided adaptive updates, and depth-conflict pruning to improve the reconstruction of newly observed surfaces.

Figure 4:Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP).
(a) Opacity-only insertion can miss new surfaces.
(b,c) Renderings without and with DAEP. Red dots mark the initial centers of Gaussians added over five neighboring keyframes.
Blue dashed boxes highlight the rear facade.
